Roadmap

Where the project is going

The labels below separate what works today, what is built but still off by default, and what is only an idea. They reflect the state of the code: if a capability is off by default, backed by a single provider, or only a setting and a name, it is described that way.

Shipped

Working, and in use

These are implemented and available today. The features page covers them in detail.

Shipped

Core conversation

Communities, channels and categories, direct messages, friends, reactions, attachments, search, presence and in-app notifications.

Shipped

Community and platform moderation

Roles and permissions, invites, reports, warnings, timeouts and bans, appeals, announcements, and a platform administration surface.

Shipped

Accounts and data rights

Registration with optional approval, two-factor authentication, email verification and recovery, data export and account deletion.

Shipped

Self-hosting

Docker and manual installs, SQLite or MySQL, mail through SMTP or an API, public discovery, bots and webhooks, themes, and the desktop app.

In progress

Built, but off by default

These have real code behind them and are deliberately off by default. They stay off until the work is finished.

Voice and video In progress

The room and signalling model exist behind one provider, with participant limits, optional screen sharing and stage channels. It is off by default and there is no second provider. Turn it on if you want to test it; do not plan a product around it yet.

Push notifications to devices In progress

The flag and the delivery plumbing exist and default to off. Notifications are dependable in-app today. A notification that reliably wakes a backgrounded phone is a different piece of work, and it is not done.

Planned and exploratory

Ideas with a name, not a date

Something here may change shape or may not arrive. Treat it as direction, not as a schedule.

Exploratory

Cross-instance federation

Instances are independent today, and there is a global sync setting and the beginning of a shared vocabulary for connecting them. A working federation of separate instances does not exist yet.

Planned

Messaging polish

Continued work on the everyday surfaces: message editing and history, richer notification controls, and the small things that make a long conversation easier to follow.

Planned

Operator experience

More of the deployment lifecycle in one place: clearer upgrade and backup guidance, and fewer places where an operator has to read the source to find out what a setting does.

Not currently planned

Things it is fair to assume are not coming

A central hosted service

Trycord is software you run. There is an official instance, but the architecture does not assume a single company in the middle, and that is not going to change into the usual arrangement.

Advertising or data brokerage

There is no advertising surface and no plan to build one. An instance's data belongs to the instance, and there is no mechanism to send it anywhere else.

Have a say

The roadmap is a conversation, not an announcement.

If something here matters to you, or you think the ordering is wrong, the support page explains where to say so.
